title: Local AWS stand-ins with Docker Compose

user_story.i_want: one `docker compose up` that starts free stand-ins for S3, SQS, DynamoDB and Postgres with buckets and queues pre-created
user_story.so_that: I can develop the whole pipeline offline and for free

description: Create `deploy/docker-compose.yml` with four services: RustFS (S3), ElasticMQ native image (SQS), DynamoDB Local (run with `-sharedDb`) and Postgres. Use named volumes, healthchecks and pinned image tags (not `latest`). ElasticMQ queues are declared in its config file: `raw-files` and `transform`, each with a DLQ (`maxReceiveCount = 5`) and a 60 s default visibility timeout. A one-shot bootstrap container creates the S3 buckets `stratum-raw` and `stratum-staged`. The `amazon/aws-cli` image means you don't need the AWS CLI on your machine. DynamoDB tables are created later by STR-401. Ports are listed in docs/aws-alternatives.md.

acceptance_criteria.then: all four infrastructure containers report healthy within 60 s
raw-files, raw-files-dlq, transform and transform-dlq exist, and raw-files has a redrive policy to its DLQ with maxReceiveCount 5

acceptance_criteria.when: I connect with psql using the credentials from `.env`

acceptance_criteria.then: Postgres and RustFS data are still there; `down -v` wipes them
`.env` is ignored and `.env.example` is committed with dev-only values

technical_notes: RustFS runs as UID 10001, so named volumes avoid bind-mount permission issues.
DynamoDB Local without `-sharedDb` keeps a separate database per access key and region: a classic 'my table vanished' trap.
Set your own RustFS access/secret keys; don't use the well-known defaults.
